article.title: Why Saving a Small Example Makes Future Work Faster
article.why: 用可重用的小範例降低未來重新摸索的成本。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A small example can save a surprising amount of time. Imagine that you have just finished a task that you do only once every few months. Maybe you cleaned a data file, changed a setting, or used a difficult formula. You understand the steps today, but you may forget them later.

Before you close the task, save one small working example. The example should show the input, the action, and the expected result. It does not need to explain everything. Its job is to give your future self a quick starting point.

For example, suppose you learned how to convert a date in a spreadsheet. Instead of writing a long manual, keep one row with the original value, the formula, and the correct output. Next time, you can copy the pattern and adapt it. This is often faster than searching old messages or trying several formulas again.

A good example is especially useful when a task has a small but important detail. Perhaps a file must use UTF-8, a command needs a special option, or a report must be filtered before export. These details are easy to forget because they are not part of your daily routine.

Examples also help teams. A colleague can see what “correct” looks like without reading a long explanation first. If the example no longer works, that is useful information too: the process may have changed and the documentation needs an update.

The key is to keep the example small and easy to find. Give it a clear name and add one short note about when to use it. You are not trying to document the whole world. You are creating a shortcut from a future question to a proven answer.

The next time you solve an annoying problem, ask yourself: “Will I need to figure this out again?” If the answer might be yes, save the smallest useful example before you move on.
